dedupe_keys.name: norway optimal base for an air mobile stroke unit to extend hyperacute stroke care

description: This case study uses geospatial optimisation to choose the best base for an Air-Mobile Stroke Unit in Norway, a concept that puts stroke diagnosis equipment on an aircraft so rural patients can be assessed before reaching hospital. The authors published it as an open-access journal article. All Norwegian helicopter emergency medical service bases were candidate sites; demand came from the 2022 Norwegian Stroke Registry at postal-code level, excluding postal codes within a 15-minute drive of a hospital, and a maximum coverage model measured how many patients could reach hyperacute treatment within 4.5 hours of onset. Coverage is national. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: flying weather, aircraft availability and costs are not modelled, and coverage is a proxy for clinical benefit. The study found that the best overall base raised the share of patients eligible for hyperacute treatment from 91.8 to 94.8 percent, while for rural patients more than 150 minutes from a hospital the best base was Harstad in northern Norway, raising the total to 97.2 percent. Simulation uses: an example of optimisation for capacity planning and investment appraisal of air emergency services. Related records: the Iceland helicopter base study (case_study-iceland-helicopter-ambulance-base-location) addresses a similar problem.
